title: Quant profile identity and catalog reconciliation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: As quantization artifacts (FP8/INT8 profiles, calibration snapshots, quant manifests) are created and promoted across environments, the catalog occasionally accumulates divergent identities for effectively identical artifacts (e.g., different manifest IDs when calibration order changes, duplicate calibration snapshots from parallel masters, or hash mismatches stemming from non-deterministic metadata like timestamps). This makes rollbacks and cross-region failover brittle, complicates MRCA (most recent correct artifact) selection, and breaks deterministic replay for calibration-based validation.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic identity scheme is defined that yields stable IDs for quant artifacts when content is semantically identical despite cosmetic metadata diffs.
A reconciliation service runs in the catalog to detect and merge duplicate artifact identities, preserving provenance and signatures.
Rollback operations can select the correct fallback artifact across Dedicated/Private clusters even when previous imports created duplicate identities.
CI regression tests verify reproducible hashing on canonical golden calibration sets for FP8 and INT8 calibration artifacts.
Operator runbook for signature rotation and repair is documented with example CLI commands and required telemetry checks.
technical_notes: Hashing: adopt content-addressing based on a canonical serialization that excludes volatile fields (created_at, ephemeral host metadata). Use SHA-256 over the canonical bytes, then base32-encode for human readability. Hash input order: model-spec -> quant-config -> calibration-goldenset-digest -> deterministic-calibration-summary -> optional transform metadata (sorted by key).

Canonical serialization: JSON with stable key ordering and normalized floats (round-trip to 8 decimal places for calibration metrics). We will implement a helper 'qcanon' used by calibration tooling and CI.

Signature: retain existing artifact signing but attach both signed_manifest_id and content_address as first-class fields. Signatures verified against KMS; create migration job to attach content_address to historical artifacts and produce signed attestations.

Reconciliation service: periodic job (daily) that groups artifacts by content_address, then reconciles duplicate manifests by selecting a primary based on: (1) highest verification status, (2) most complete calibration metrics, (3) creation_time earliest. The service must not delete historical manifests; instead it creates an alias map and writes reconciliation events to an append-only ledger for auditability.

Rollback semantics: rollback operations should prefer content_address selection rather than manifest ID. The Console and runtime APIs need a compatibility layer that accepts either manifest_id or content_address. The orchestration must ensure pinned model versions map to content_address and that model-serving workers can fetch by either identifier.
Multi-region replication: reconciliation must be idempotent and tolerant of eventual consistency; use CRDT-friendly merges for alias maps and provide conflict resolution logs.

Calibration reproducibility tests: define two canonical golden-sets (one for FP8 workloads, one for INT8) stored in immutable buckets; CI will run qcanon + calibration harness and verify resulting content_address equals recorded golden hash.

Backward compatibility: a migration job will compute content_address for all existing artifacts and store as 'content_address_v1'; until all consumers switch, maintain both fields. Deprecation window: 3 months post-release.

Operator CLI examples included in runbook: 'rw-quant reconcile --since 2026-01-01 --dry-run', 'rw-quant compute-hash --input calibration.json', 'rw-quant attach-alias --primary <content_address> --alias <manifest_id>'.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Implement qcanon library in Python/Go, include stable serializer and float normalization. Add unit tests for edge cases (NaNs, infinities, metadata ordering).
Week 2: Add content_address field to new artifacts; update calibration pipeline to compute and attach. Add CI tests that validate content_address on golden sets.
Week 3: Build reconciliation service (k8s CronJob + idempotent worker) with dry-run mode and audit ledger writes to blob store.
Week 4: Add compatibility layer in catalog API and runtime fetch path; implement migration job for historical artifacts and run in staging (monitor for anomalies).
Week 5: Update Console and rollout UI to display content_address and alias relationships; add operator runbook and train SRE on repair steps.
Contingency: if migration reveals >0.1% hash collisions, pause migration and engage Research to examine normalization tolerances.
test_plan: Unit tests for qcanon serializer: stable ordering and float normalization cases.
Integration test: create identical artifacts with different ephemeral metadata and assert content_address equal and reconciliation aliases created.
Performance test: compute content_address for 10k artifacts in < 5 minutes in migration job (scale-out ok).
End-to-end CI: run FP8 and INT8 golden calibrations in a reproducible environment; verify content_address matches recorded golden hash; fail pipeline on mismatch.
Chaos test: while reconciliation running, simulate concurrent artifact writes and ensure alias map converges.
Manual QA: SRE runbook drill—simulate signature rotation and use CLI to remap aliases and validate runtime can fetch by content_address.

operational_runbook: Initial validation: run 'rw-quant compute-hash --input <artifact.json>' and compare against catalog 'content_address' field.
Dry-run reconciliation: 'rw-quant reconcile --since <date> --dry-run' to produce alias suggestions. Review audit ledger at /audit/quant/reconcile/YYYYMMDD.log.
Rollback reconciliation: the reconcile job writes an invertible ledger; to undo, 'rw-quant reconcile --apply --ledger <ledger-id> --revert'.

Signature rotation repair: compute new content_address, re-sign via KMS, then use attach-alias to map old manifest IDs to new content_address. Ensure replication to all regions and run 'rw-quant verify-signatures --since <date>'.
